measurements.environment: Windows local workspace; warm filesystem cache; observational timings are evidence, not portable certification thresholds.
measurements.interpretation: The snapshot removes normal dashboard replay work, but exclusive FileLock lease writes and fsyncs dominate the cached read. Append still retains full-stream and whole-file work.

findings.title: Append remains full-stream and whole-file
findings.observation: Every append reads all events, projects the current stream, projects the stream plus the candidate again, reads all existing ledger bytes, and atomically rewrites the complete JSONL.
findings.impact: Sequential imports are quadratic in accumulated ledger size and append latency grows continuously.

findings.title: Snapshot reads take the mutating exclusive lock
findings.observation: read_snapshot acquires FileLock, whose lease acquisition and release write and fsync lock metadata.
findings.impact: Dashboard reads contend with writers and pay control-plane write latency even though snapshot publication is atomic.

findings.title: Compact snapshot check is not full-chain verification
findings.observation: The cached path checks a snapshot self-hash, ledger size, and final event. A same-length corruption in an earlier event can leave all three unchanged.
findings.impact: The cached result must be represented as checkpoint-bound, not fully replay-verified, and must not seed mutation without a verified checkpoint and unchanged ledger fingerprint.

findings.title: Snapshot write bound is enforced only on read
findings.observation: The writer does not reject an encoded snapshot larger than MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES before publication; the next reader rejects it.
findings.impact: A successful append can publish a snapshot that makes the dashboard fail closed immediately afterward.

findings.title: Automatic ID allocation scans the full stream
findings.observation: AUTO gap allocation scans all discovered-card events for every new card.
findings.impact: Automatic allocation adds avoidable linear work and should use checkpointed maximum ordinal state.

findings.title: Current concurrency evidence is thread-only
findings.observation: The current test uses ThreadPoolExecutor, so it does not exercise independent process leases, process death, or Windows cross-process byte locks.
findings.impact: The multi-process safety claim is not yet independently demonstrated.

findings.title: Default dashboard projection still hydrates the full detailed snapshot
findings.observation: Although rows are paginated after loading, the default dashboard parses all detailed cards, histories, surfaces, reports, and evidence.
findings.impact: Startup cost remains proportional to the full derived state instead of the requested first page and compact progress metadata.

findings.title: True append requires explicit torn-tail recovery
findings.observation: The current whole-file atomic replace avoids torn append records. Replacing it with direct append without a receipt-bound tail recovery protocol would weaken crash behavior.
findings.impact: Performance repair must preserve complete valid events, quarantine invalid suffix bytes, and truncate only proven uncommitted bytes.

architecture_recommendations.authoritative_boundary: Keep registry/operational_gap_ledger.jsonl as the sole authority. Snapshot and head files remain deterministic, derived, bounded, and rebuildable.
shared_reducer: Refactor project_events around one ProjectionState reducer with empty, restore-from-checkpoint, apply-event, and render operations.
Use the same reducer for full replay, incremental append, batch append, and recovery so semantic validation cannot drift between paths.
Render incremental and full-replay snapshots byte-identically after sealing metadata is normalized.

compact_head_checkpoint.admission_rule: A checkpoint may seed mutation only if it originated from a full verified replay and its file identity, metadata, committed offset, tail sequence, and tail hash still match. Any mismatch requires replay or explicit recovery.
compact_head_checkpoint.trust_boundary: A project-local self-hash is hash binding, not protection from an attacker who can rewrite every project file. Stronger authentication requires an external signing or OS-protected trust anchor.

append_path: Acquire the existing cross-process FileLock exactly once.
Load an admitted checkpoint or perform full replay/recovery.
Prepare and validate the candidate against the shared reducer before persistence.
Enforce fixed event and total-ledger byte bounds before writing.
Append only the encoded event through an exact-write loop, then flush and fsync the ledger.
Apply the event once to in-memory state.
Atomically publish the deterministic full snapshot.
Publish the compact head last as the coherent checkpoint commit marker.
batch_path: Add append_events or a bounded ledger session that acquires one lock, loads or replays once, validates events sequentially, appends them in order, and publishes one final snapshot/head.
Use the batch path for initialization, report imports, reconciliation, and multi-transition updates.
Complete hash-valid events remain authoritative if checkpoint publication fails; the next recovery incorporates them exactly once.
dashboard_path: Do not acquire the mutating exclusive lease for ordinary dashboard reads.
Use a bounded optimistic read: head A, bounded referenced data and ledger metadata/tail checks, head B; accept only when A and B match.
Serve the unfiltered startup page and progress counts directly from the compact head.
Load the full snapshot only for explicit filters, inventory detail, or card detail.
Return checkpoint_stale or recovery_required on disagreement; never label stale cached data current and never run full replay in foreground dashboard startup.
recovery_path: Start from the last admitted committed byte offset and head hash.
Accept only complete, sequential, content-hash-valid and previous-hash-valid tail events.
Before truncating a torn or invalid suffix, preserve its exact bytes or content hash in a recovery artifact and fsync a receipt.
Never discard a complete valid event and never silently repair authoritative bytes.
After recovery, rebuild the deterministic snapshot and publish a new compact head.
explicit_non_recommendations: Do not introduce SQLite or event-directory sharding for this repair; the shared reducer, real append, checkpoint, and bounded dashboard page are the smaller sufficient seam.
Do not maintain a separate permissive fast-path validator; it would create semantic drift.
Do not call a self-hashed project-local snapshot externally authenticated.

targeted_tests.assertion: After every supported event type, incremental output is byte-identical to a full replay snapshot after normalization of seal metadata.
A warm admitted append does not call _read_events_unlocked or project_events and does not read existing ledger bytes.
The ledger grows by exactly the encoded event length and preexisting bytes remain byte-identical.
A bounded multi-event append loads or replays once and publishes one coherent checkpoint.
A same-length earlier-event mutation invalidates checkpoint admission, and full validation rejects the event hash or chain.
Snapshot tampering, head tampering, stale size, stale fingerprint, and head/snapshot disagreement all fail closed.
Failure after ledger fsync but before snapshot/head publication preserves the complete event and incorporates it exactly once during recovery.
Recovery quarantines the exact invalid suffix, produces a hash-bound receipt, truncates only uncommitted bytes, and preserves the previous head.
Independent subprocess writers produce contiguous sequences, continuous previous hashes, no event loss, and a replay-equal snapshot.
A dashboard read concurrent with append returns either the old complete checkpoint or the new complete checkpoint, never a hybrid.
The unfiltered startup request reads only the bounded compact head/page, never replays the ledger, and respects the declared size and latency budget.
Oversized event, ledger, full snapshot, compact head, and recovery delta fail before unsafe publication.
AUTO allocation uses checkpointed maximum ordinal state and remains identical after replay and recovery.
Repeated checkpoint construction and replay/incremental construction produce identical snapshot and compact-head bytes.

gpu_parallel_disposition.reason: Ledger mutation, hash-chain ordering, filesystem durability, cleanup, and recovery are CPU-authoritative ordered control-plane work. GPU setup or parallel mutation would add transfer, synchronization, and correctness risk without useful acceleration.
safe_concurrency: Parallelize independent evidence collection before ordered event admission.
Serialize admitted event publication under the cross-process lock.
Use batching and incremental reduction, not unordered parallel projection, for throughput.

completion_disposition.reason: The current partial snapshot fast path improves dashboard replay cost but append remains quadratic, reads remain lock/fsync-heavy, checkpoint trust is incomplete, and crash-safe true append is not implemented.
